mgmt_bio.text: Vasant "Vas" Narasimhan, M.D., has been chief executive officer of Novartis since February 1, 2018. Born in Pittsburgh in 1976, he studied biological sciences at the University of Chicago, earned an M.D. from Harvard Medical School and a master's degree in public policy from Harvard's Kennedy School. He worked as a consultant at McKinsey & Company before joining Novartis in 2005, rising to Global Head of Drug Development and Chief Medical Officer from 2016 to 2018. As CEO he has refocused the group as a medicines company and leads more than 77,000 associates doing business in about 120 countries, and over his career has overseen approval of more than 35 novel medicines and vaccines. In April 2026 he also joined the board of the AI company Anthropic.

sentences.text: Vas Narasimhan has led Novartis since February 2018 and has refocused it from a diversified healthcare group into a pure-play medicines company, completing the Sandoz spin-off in 2023 after divesting Alcon.

Execution showed in Q2 2025, with sales up 11% and core operating income up 21%, while 2025 buybacks totalled USD 8.9 billion across the completed USD 15 billion programme and a new up-to USD 10 billion authorisation and the board proposed a 29th consecutive dividend increase, to CHF 3.70.

sentences.quote: Net sales were USD 14.4 billion (+3%, +1% cc), with volume growth contributing 18 percentage points, offset by 14 percentage points from generic competition.
sentences.text: Novartis AG has returned to sales growth after absorbing US generic erosion, with Q2 2026 net sales of USD 14.4 billion, up 1 percent in constant currencies.
Growth is carried by a broad set of priority brands including Kisqali, Kesimpta, Scemblix, Pluvicto and Leqvio, which offset Entresto generic competition.
Management counts eight de-risked, in-market assets with peak sales potential of USD 3-10 billion: Kisqali, Cosentyx, Kesimpta, Pluvicto, Scemblix, Leqvio, Fabhalta and Rhapsido.
Mid-term guidance runs to 2030 with a sales CAGR of 5-6 percent in constant currencies, supported by 15 or more potentially submission-enabling readouts over the next two years.
